chunks: Abu Al-Abbas Al-Razzaz, from Ayoub ibn Nuh, and Humayd ibn Ziyad, from Ibn Sama'ah, from Safwan, from Ibn Muskan, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
When a man divorces his wife before consummating the marriage with her, with one irrevocable divorce, she becomes separated from him, and she may marry immediately if she wishes.

key_terms.دَخَلَ بِهَا: consummated the marriage / entered with her

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on divorce before consummation in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies that a single pronouncement of divorce before consummation (dakhala) results in an immediate, irrevocable separation, allowing the wife to remarry instantly without observing the waiting period (iddah). This ruling is derived from the principle that the primary purpose of iddah in this context is to ascertain potential pregnancy, which is impossible prior to cohabitation. It highlights the distinct Shia jurisprudential view on the finality of this specific type of divorce compared to other schools of thought.

en.hubeali:
Abu Al Abbas Al Razzaz, from Ayoub Bin Nuh, and Humeyd Bin Ziyad, from Ibn Sama’at, from Safwan, from Ibn Muskan, from Abu Baseer, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘When the man divorces his wife before he sleeping with her, one divorce, she is irrevocably divorced from him, and she can marry from that very moment if she so desires to’.
en.sarwar: 6. Abu al-‘Abbas al-Razzaz has narrated from Ayyub ibn Nuh and Humayd ibn Ziyad from ibn Sama‘ah from Safwan from ibn Muskan from abu Basir who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘
If a man divorces his wife before going to bed with her with one divorce, she becomes stranger to him in the same hour after divorce. She can marry someone if she wants.’”
